data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘समीरः’ (samīraḥ), meaning ‘admirer’, ‘worshiper’, or ‘lover’. In Hindu mythology, the name is associated with the god Indra, who is known for his passion and courage. It is also believed to bring admiration and love from others. The name समीर carries the meaning “Admirer, Lover” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose समीर usually hope their child will grow to embody admirer, lover and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference:
Samirasura, also known as Shinganakia or Shishupal, was a powerful Asura king who was a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He was the younger brother of King Bali, who ruled over the nether world. According to Hindu mythology, Samirasura was defeated by Lord Krishna in a battle, after which he surrendered to him and attained salvation. This event is described in the Mahabharata and the Puranas.
Time period: 3000 BCE - 2000 BCE
Context: Hindu mythology and epics

Samantasimha, also known as Samiravarman, was a Chalukya king who ruled over the Karnataka region in the south of India during the 10th century CE. He was a powerful warrior and is known for his victory over the Chola king Paranthaka I at the Battle of Talikota. This battle marked the end of the Early Chola Empire and the rise of the Chalukya Empire.
Time period: 973 CE - 997 CE
Context: Indian history and medieval warfare
